keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1887-1889: Cliopatria starts in 1890, but 'In 1887, the Anglo-French Joint Naval Commission took charge of the territory' (after the 1878 declaration that the UK and France made all the New Hebrides neutral territory). The shape is the whole archipelago (Natural Earth Vanuatu). Franceville (an area around present-day Port Vila) broke away from 9 August 1889 to June 1890: see the ledger. Reviewer oc-02-a (2026-10-18): the Cliopatria shape covers only 28 of the 43 land cells of Natural Earth Vanuatu, the missing cells spread over every province (coasts of Espiritu Santo, Pentecost, Maewo, the Banks, Tanna, Erromango, Aneityum), so the correction is the whole archipelago, as in the found event.

region.text: the New Hebrides, the islands of modern Vanuatu

ledger.note: 1887: Britain and France take joint charge of the New Hebrides. 'In 1887, the Anglo-French Joint Naval Commission took charge of the territory' (periods 1887-1889 and 1890-1906); in 1878 'the United Kingdom and France declared all of the New Hebrides to be neutral territory'. The page names the territory, not its islands.

region.text: Franceville, 'an area around present-day Port Vila'

ledger.note: 1889: Franceville declares itself an independent commune. 'An area around present-day Port Vila, declared itself an independent commune' (9 August 1889), led by an elected president.

region.text: Franceville, 'an area around present-day Port Vila'

ledger.note: 1890: the Naval Commission resumes control. 'By June 1890, Franceville as a commune was reported to have been "practically broken up"', after which the Joint Naval Commission resumed control.

1906: the Anglo-French Condominium replaces the Joint Naval Commission. Infobox 'Established: 20 October 1906'; the Protocol of 1906 'became effective in 1907' and 'provided for joint sovereignty over the archipelago with two parallel administrations, one British, one French'.
1980: the New Hebrides become the Republic of Vanuatu. 'Independence: 30 July 1980'; internal self-government had come in January 1978.

certainty.note: An island archipelago; the coast is the border. Sovereignty was shared (two parallel administrations), which the border does not show.

sources.title: New Hebrides
sources.note: Joint Naval Commission 1887, Franceville 1889-1890, Condominium 20 October 1906, internal self-government January 1978, independence 30 July 1980, capital Port Vila. No area on the page. Opened twice (second time for Franceville and the French name).

notes:
Written 2026-10-18 from one page (budget 1-2). Type colony: a dependency ruled jointly from London and Paris, so the metropoles' dossiers (british-colonial-empire; french-third-republic, french-fourth-republic, french-fifth-republic) should record the condominium as a shared vassal/colony relation with counterpart new-hebrides, and neither should also hold the land directly. Not on the page: the 1942-1945 American base on Espiritu Santo (only a related-link title), the 1980 Santo rebellion / Nagriamel secession (absent), the 1914 protocol and 1922 ratification, the area, the number of islands. A gap-filler should open 'Anglo-French Condominium' (if a separate page exists) and 'Coconut War' for the 1980 secession.

Cliopatria: 'New Hebrides' 1890-1982 against independence on 30 July 1980; the Vanuatu row (oc-02-b) begins in 1983, leaving 1981-1982 to this row: the verdict on the 1979 shape cuts it at July 1980. The slug 'vanuatu' belongs to batch oc-02-b. Franceville is a counterpart named in words because it lasted under a year and has no page opened beyond the New Hebrides article.
